contract.words: Collect $1,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: Target settled cash received within the window

strategy.title: List an allergen-labelled meal-plan workbook at $29 on the digital-download marketplace and sell 39 copies in 30 days
strategy.why: Price ($29 listing prices, 2026-11), buyer volume (2,300 comparable sales in 12 months across 40 sellers), channel (marketplace listing and search), Brain-produced spreadsheet delivery, $3 direct cost and 3-day time to first cash are all evidenced. 39 sales gross $1,131 and net $1,014 after $117 of direct costs, paid from receipts, so no up-front capital is used. What is not established is how many sales a new listing wins: the 2,300/yr market is ~190/month across 40 sellers (~5 per seller), so 39 in 30 days needs a new listing to take ~20% of a month's category sales. That rate is measured by a live listing test before scaling effort.

alternatives.title: Lower price to win more of the category volume
alternatives.why: Lower price needs more sales from the same ~190/month category volume; no evidence that price drives share.

validation.proof: By day 10 the listing has at least 13 settled sales (pace for 39 in 30 days).
stop: Fewer than 5 settled sales by day 10: the listing cannot take the share needed; stop and re-plan.
Marketplace fees push net per sale below the $1,000 target at 39 sales and no price/volume fix exists.
continue: 13 or more settled sales by day 10: continue selling to 39.
5-12 sales by day 10: continue only with a listing change and re-measure by day 17.

strategy.title: List an allergen-labelled meal-plan workbook at $29 on the digital-download marketplace and sell 50 copies in 30 days, sized on net payout
strategy.why: Price ($29 listing prices, 2026-11), category volume (2,300 comparable sales in 12 months across 40 sellers), channel (listing and search), Brain-produced spreadsheet delivery, $3 direct cost and 3-day time to first cash are evidenced. The marketplace seller fee is not on the record, so the plan is sized on payout net of an assumed fee ceiling of 20%: 50 sales pay out $1,160 and net $1,010 after $150 of direct costs, all paid from receipts (no up-front capital). The fee is read from the marketplace's published seller terms on day 0, before any sale; above 20% the plan stops. The new listing's sales rate is the live unknown: 50 sales in 30 days is about 26% of the ~190/month category and roughly 10 times the ~5/month average seller. No second opening exists on the record to diversify, so the plan carries no hidden assumption — the day-10 test stops it early if the pace is not met.

alternatives.title: Run at 39 sales gross
alternatives.why: Rejected: gross $29 is not settled cash; any fee above ~11.6% drops 39 sales below $1,000, and net of costs it had only $14 headroom.

alternatives.title: Add a second opening for buffer
alternatives.why: No second opening exists in this world's record; Brain should keep constructing openings in parallel.

alternatives.title: Lower price to win share
alternatives.why: No evidence price drives share; lower price needs even more sales.
